teams.name: Mexico
teams.sub: Round of 16 · out to England at the Azteca
teams.blurb: The tournament’s meanest group-stage defence: five matches, one goal conceded. England finally solved the block at the Azteca in the Round of 16.

teams.name: Brazil
teams.sub: Third place · beat Spain in the bronze final
teams.blurb: Bronze medalists. Slow starts and big finishes. The five-goal semi-final against France was the match of the tournament, and they took third on the final weekend.

teams.name: Morocco
teams.sub: Quarter-finalists · only the champions beat them
teams.blurb: Organized chaos for opponents, calm for Morocco. They beat the Netherlands on penalties and shut out Canada. Only the eventual champions ended the run, 2–1 in the quarter-final.

teams.name: United States
teams.sub: Round of 16 · out on penalties to Belgium
teams.blurb: The hosts pressed in packs and scored off turnovers, but the run ended on penalties against Belgium while the suspended Balogun watched from the stands.

teams.name: France
teams.sub: World Champions · beat Argentina 3–1 in the final
teams.blurb: Champions by counterattack. France conceded possession all tournament and broke at pace through Mbappé and Olise, scoring 18 goals in seven matches. Mbappé’s brace in the final capped the run.

teams.name: Norway
teams.blurb: Route one, refined. Haaland’s five goals carried Norway through the group and past Ivory Coast before Brazil ended the run in the Round of 16.

teams.name: Argentina
teams.sub: Runners-up · lost the final 1–3 to France
teams.blurb: A title defence that fell one match short. Argentina went unbeaten until the final, with Messi producing five goals and six assists at 39, before France’s pace on the break decided East Rutherford.

players.name: Lionel Messi
players.note: GOLDEN BALL · PLAYER OF THE TOURNAMENT

stadiums.blurb: Canada's west-coast host, a downtown bowl under a retractable roof. Canada beat Qatar 6–0 here in the group stage.
Temporarily expanded from its MLS footprint for the tournament. Canada opened its home World Cup here with a 1–1 draw against Bosnia & Herzegovina.
The final. Spain beat Argentina 1–0 here on 19 July to win the World Cup.
Nine matches, more than any other venue, including the semi-final where Spain beat France 2–0.
The United States opened here with a 4–1 win over Paraguay, then lost 3–2 to Türkiye on the same pitch to close the group stage.
The oldest of the American venues, and the loudest: it holds the Guinness record for crowd noise at an outdoor stadium.
Six matches in the South Bay, among them the United States' 2–0 Round of 32 win over Bosnia & Herzegovina.
A climate-controlled Gulf Coast venue. Morocco ended Canada's run here, 3–0 in the Round of 16.
Six matches through the group stage and knockouts, on the tournament's north-east corridor.
Eight matches under the pinwheel roof, ending with Argentina's 2–1 semi-final win over England.
The Pacific Northwest host, where Belgium knocked the United States out 4–1 in the Round of 16.
Host of the third-place play-off, a 6–4 to England over France — the highest-scoring match of the tournament.
Seven matches at the New England venue, from the group stage through to a quarter-final.
The only stadium to host three World Cups — 1970, 1986 and 2026 — and the opening match, Mexico 2–0 South Africa. Known locally as Estadio Banorte under its current sponsorship.
Set against the Cerro de la Silla ridge, the newest of the three Mexican venues.
Mexico's second home in the group stage, where they beat South Korea 1–0.
